definitions.explanation: To a degree that is clearly distinguishable from the previous state or from other things being compared. Emphasizes that the difference is substantial.

examples.japanese: {技術|ぎじゅつ}が{格段|かくだん}に{上|あ}がった。
{去年|きょねん}より{格段|かくだん}に{良|よ}い{成績|せいせき}を{取|と}った。
examples.english: I got significantly better grades than last year.

examples.japanese: スマートフォンの{性能|せいのう}は{十年前|じゅうねんまえ}と{比|くら}べて{格段|かくだん}に{向上|こうじょう}している。
examples.english: Smartphone performance has improved dramatically compared to ten years ago.

notes:
Typically modifies verbs or adjectives that describe improvement, difference, or change. Almost always implies a positive or upward change.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {格段|かくだん}に{良|よ}い (remarkably better)
- {格段|かくだん}に{上|あ}がる (to rise significantly)
- {格段|かくだん}に{向上|こうじょう}する (to improve dramatically)
- {格段|かくだん}に{違|ちが}う (to be notably different)

USAGE:
{格段|かくだん}に emphasizes that the gap or improvement is not merely slight but clearly noticeable. It is slightly more formal than ずっと or はるかに, and is common in written Japanese and formal speech.
